title: PUBG Mobile Account Listings: How to Check Cosmetic Claims and Risks
summary: Learn to read X-Suit, Gun Lab, rank and car-skin claims without mistaking screenshots for verified ownership.
intro: A PUBG Mobile account listing may advertise a long inventory of X-Suits, upgradable weapons, Mythic outfits and vehicle finishes. A headline count is not a complete account history or a guarantee of ownership. This guide explains how to evaluate the information shown and understand publisher restrictions, without encouraging password sharing, account takeovers or unsupported transfers.

sections.heading: Read every count in context
paragraphs: An account level, Mythic outfit total, number of Gun Lab weapons and vehicle finish count measure different things. A claim of 30 upgradeable guns does not mean those guns are fully upgraded. Similarly, two X-Suits can have very different visual stages. Write each field separately and leave unclear items unverified. A vague description should never be treated as proof of an exact cosmetic collection.

sections.heading: Examine item identity and progress
paragraphs: For a named M416 or AKM finish, confirm both its exact name and the stage shown in the current inventory interface. Kill-message effects, lobby appearances and elimination crates can have distinct progression requirements. A screenshot from a promotion or another account cannot demonstrate entitlement. If a seller displays a static image, it should be described as an image, not definitive proof that every item is present today.

sections.heading: Car cosmetics need specific names
paragraphs: A car-card image may not establish a transferable vehicle skin or even one permanent finish. Different branded collaborations have separate models, colors and regional event rules. Ask what is actually pictured and what the game's current interface says. A claim that every luxury vehicle can be gifted is not reliable without publisher-supported gifting rules. Do not infer account inventory simply from the presence of a popular logo.

sections.heading: Ranks and achievements are historical
paragraphs: Conqueror in a previous season is not the same as current ranked placement. Achievement titles, profile level and Royale Pass participation also describe different dimensions of progression. Confirm which season a screenshot belongs to and whether it was captured before a reset. Beware of altered, cropped or reused images. Even authentic screenshots are snapshots, so their accuracy can change after an account's status changes.

sections.heading: Understand publisher rules first
paragraphs: PUBG Mobile's license terms restrict account transfers and third-party virtual-item dealings except where explicitly permitted. That creates policy and security risk even when advertised cosmetics exist. A marketplace description cannot override publisher rules or guarantee recovery control. Do not give anyone a one-time code, device approval or recovery email access to prove interest. Keep personally identifying details private when discussing a listing.

sections.heading: Make a risk-based decision
paragraphs: Separate verified facts, unclear claims and policy restrictions into three columns. Reject claims of anti-ban protection, instant unlocks or guaranteed permanent access that lack authoritative support. If a lawful publisher-supported transaction exists, use only its published process and protections. Otherwise, the safest choice is to keep control of your own account and acquire cosmetic items through supported in-game methods.
